result.summary: The image shows a narrow residential street with continuous sidewalks and dense parallel parking on both sides. While the narrow roadway likely encourages lower vehicle speeds, the high density of parked cars creates significant visual obstructions for pedestrians attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: A continuous line of parked vehicles on both sides of the street obscures pedestrians, particularly children, from the view of oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the street view

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: The absence of marked mid-block crossings or pedestrian signage may lead to unpredictable crossing behavior in a dense residential area.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the nearest intersections to improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians and shorten crossing distances.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to physically ensure that vehicle speeds remain low in this residential environment.

result.summary: The image shows a constrained pedestrian environment with a very narrow walkway directly adjacent to a building facade and parked vehicles. There is no visible buffer between the walking area and the roadway, and sightlines for pedestrians exiting the building are obstructed by the parked cars.

hazards.name: Narrow Walkway
hazards.description: The paved area for pedestrians is extremely narrow, limiting mobility and forcing people close to parked or moving vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Between the building facade and the parked white car.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles block the sightlines for pedestrians exiting the building doors directly onto the street level.
hazards.location_in_image: The white SUV in the foreground obscures the view of the street from the building entrances.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Increase the width of the pedestrian walkway to meet standard accessibility requirements and provide a safer buffer from traffic.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking immediately adjacent to building entrances to improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extension
interventions.description: If this is near an intersection, curb extensions could be used to narrow the roadway and provide more space for pedestrians.

result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides with buildings directly at the sidewalk edge, creating a traditional urban corridor. However, the lack of visible crosswalk markings at the intersection and significant visual obstructions from parked cars reduce pedestrian safety.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street obscures sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and approaching vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs in the foreground and mid-ground.

hazards.name: Unmarked Intersection
hazards.description: The intersection ahead lacks visible high-visibility crosswalk markings, which fails to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install zebra-style crosswalk markings at all legs of the intersection to increase driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility by preventing parking at the corners.

result.summary: The environment is highly hostile to pedestrians, featuring a complete lack of dedicated sidewalk infrastructure. Pedestrians are forced to share a narrow, obstructed space between the building frontage and parked vehicles.

hazards.name: Lack of dedicated sidewalk
hazards.description: There is no separated walkway, forcing pedestrians to walk in the vehicle parking and travel area.
hazards.location_in_image: Entire foreground area between the building and the parked SUV

hazards.name: Physical obstructions
hazards.description: Construction barrels and trash containers further restrict the already limited space available for walking.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side near the orange barrel and right side near the blue and white barrels

interventions.title: Sidewalk Construction
interventions.description: Install a raised, ADA-compliant sidewalk to provide physical separation and a dedicated path for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Obstruction Removal
interventions.description: Clear the walking area of barrels, trash cans, and other debris to ensure a continuous path.

interventions.title: Parking Reconfiguration
interventions.description: Restrict or reconfigure on-street parking to reclaim space for pedestrian infrastructure and improve sightlines.
